correctness.rationale: For every nine-set of cube vertices, the compact width polar contains every inverse edge-matrix row of an enclosing parallelotope. Maximizing the multilinear determinant reduces to four polar vertices. The exact reproducible witness checks all 56 orbits of 11440 possible nine-sets, all claimed vertices and all supporting hull facets, and all 290663 four-row determinants, with maximum one. The cubic-slab counterexample at eight corners and unit-cube equality are explicit. The exact finite witness is backed by facet-completeness reasoning; finite random sampling is not invoked.

broader_coverage.reasoning: The primary theorem implies volume at least one only under its complete-facet-plus-opposite-corner incidence hypothesis. originality.rationale: The closest primary source settles all five-vertex three-cube cases and only facet-plus-opposite configurations in higher dimension, leaving arbitrary nine-vertex four-cube volume obstruction open in its statement. A parity-based nine-vertex subset has no complete facet and demonstrates that the source theorem cannot yield the universal bound by direct restriction. Searches of equivalent minimum-enclosure and determinant-width formulations, published mathematical result records, and geometric literature identified no directly covering statement. Priority remains provisional.

value.rationale: The exact four-dimensional majority threshold is a mathematically natural and sharp necessary volume consequence of an explicitly posed open lattice-covering question, in the smallest dimension beyond the published complete three-dimensional case. It settles all 56 four-cube symmetry classes, including parity patterns outside the known facet criterion. This is a substantive complete finite classification, not an arbitrary case slice or a restatement of a known bound; it does not purport to prove lattice covering.
